correctness.rationale: Reconstructed for the stated d>p+2 and p not dividing B=d−1. At s=1/u=0 the equation is v^p+sv=sf(1/s). Any root has negative valuation, so the p-th power term uniquely dominates sv and v has s-valuation −B/p. The denominator forces local degree and ramification p; this also proves irreducibility and leaves one place above infinity. The affine derivative in v is 1. For finite u and a pole of v, b=1/v gives u+b^(p−1)=f(u)b^p, which forces u=0 and has one smooth formal solution with u=−b^(p−1)+O(b^p). Both places map to [0:1:0]; losing the affine chart requires a pole of u or v, so the list is exhaustive. In (a,b)=(u/v,1/v) the orders are (p,1) and (A,B), A=B−p>1. Extraction of an A-th root of a unit yields a=t^A; in the cusp branch's Weierstrass basis 1,b,…,b^(A−1) over k[[a]], the summands have distinct valuation classes mod A. Thus the cusp semigroup is exactly <A,B>; the smooth branch equation a=−b^p+O(b^(p+1)) has order A on it. Its semigroup gaps number (A−1)(B−1)/2. The intersection adds A to delta and to each intrinsic conductor exponent, since elements supported on one component are the other component's equation times elements of the branch ring, and the maximal normalization ideal contained there is that factor times the branch conductor. This gives total delta, genus, the stated (3,2) example and the two rational places over the prime field (both individually Frobenius-fixed). Reviewed the integer checks as limited corroboration, not a source of the branch proof.
